text:
alex: Quick heads-up — ran a targeted micro-run comparing L4 vs T4 vs A10G for embeddings (512-d) and a small-chat workload (max_len=256). Regions: us-west1, eu-west1, ap-southeast1. Posting highlights and raw snippets.

maria: awesome, drop the perf table pls. did you include q4 quant?

alex: included q4_0 and q8_0 for comparison on small-chat; embeddings mostly Q8_0. Kept batching conservative to mimic PLG tail: max_batch=8, micro-batch window=50ms.

bench-bot: [run started] 2323456789 — config: model=v-next-small, seqs=1000 per region, concurrent=48, warmup=200

sam: curious about kernels — which ones did you pick? triton/flash/fused?

alex: kernel choices per GPU: A10G -> flash_attn + fused-gemm fallback; L4 -> optimized-fused (vendor kernel) + kv-cache tweaks; T4 -> triton fallback + slower gelu path. I pinned T4 to triton v2.3.

kevin: paste the p50/p95 and tokens/sec for each region?

alex: short table (p50 / p95 / tok/s / $ per 1M tokens - small-chat):
```
us-west1:
  L4:  p50=28ms  p95=110ms  tok/s=520  $/1M=3.10
  A10G: p50=22ms  p95=90ms   tok/s=740  $/1M=2.35
  T4:  p50=45ms  p95=210ms  tok/s=260  $/1M=1.50

eu-west1:
  L4:  p50=31ms  p95=120ms  tok/s=480  $/1M=3.30
  A10G: p50=24ms  p95=95ms   tok/s=700  $/1M=2.45
  T4:  p50=48ms  p95=220ms  tok/s=240  $/1M=1.55

ap-southeast1:
  L4:  p50=35ms  p95=128ms  tok/s=440  $/1M=3.40
  A10G: p50=26ms  p95=100ms  tok/s=680  $/1M=2.55
  T4:  p50=52ms  p95=230ms  tok/s=220  $/1M=1.60
```

maria: embeddings (512d) numbers? those change cost calculus a lot.

alex: embeddings throughput (req/sec, since tokens≈1k avg per request):
```
us-west1:
  L4:  320 req/s  p95 latency=140ms  $/1M vecs=4.2
  A10G: 480 req/s  p95=95ms    $/1M vecs=3.1
  T4:  150 req/s  p95=300ms    $/1M vecs=2.0
```

sam: so T4 still cheapest per-unit but much worse latency — classic tradeoff. any quality regressions with q4?

alex: small-chat quality (BLEU-ish proxy / safety token match) - relative delta vs fp16 baseline:
- Q8_0: ~0.0% change (negligible)
- Q4_0: ~-1.2% on small-chat prompts (noticeable for system prompts + few-shot)
- embeddings: Q4_0 ≈ -0.05% cosine delta (safe)
So embeddings OK with aggressive quant; small-chat less so depending on prompt type.

kevin: region weirdness? storage / nvlink differences?

alex: observed higher p95 on eu-west1 L4 due to a bad kernel placement — some nodes were on older kernel driver (nvml mismatch). Fix was to force kernel=optimized-fused on those nodes; p95 dropped ~18ms. Note: T4 fleet had heterogenous firmware, which explains the long tail in ap-southeast1.

bench-bot: [artifact] logs -> s3://redwood-bench/2323456789/ (csv + raw traces)

maria: any notes on batching and prefix caching?

alex: yes — enabling prefix/KV caching for small-chat reduced p95 by ~25% for repeat-prefix workloads (we simulated 40% prefix reuse). Continuous batching beyond 50ms window increased tok/s but added 10-30ms latency headroom; for PLG frontends I recommend window=30-50ms.

sam: cost-performance takeaway for product teams? short blurb pls.

alex: TL;DR: if latency is primary (interactive small-chat), A10G is the sweet spot — best p50/p95 and good tok/s; L4 is close on latency but ~30-40% higher cost for embeddings; T4 is cheapest but high tail latency — good for async bulk embeddings or batch inference. Use Q4_0 for embeddings to save cost; avoid Q4_0 for sensitive small-chat prompts unless you accept ~1% quality drop.

kevin: action items?

alex: 1) Add kernel pin checklist for eu-west L4 nodes (PR in infra). 2) Add a policy recommendation doc for customers: "When to pick T4 vs A10G vs L4" (I'll draft). 3) Expose a quick toggle in runtime to prefer prefix caching for routes with heavy prefix reuse.

maria: thx, can you attach the perf CSV for the embedding runs to the ticket?

alex: uploaded to the bench-bot S3 link. creating infra + docs PRs now.

kevin: nice. one more ask — can we run a 1-hour soak with production-like concurrent spikes (1000c) on A10G to verify no mem leakage? schedule?

alex: yes, scheduling for tomorrow night in us-west1 low-traffic window. I'll post results. :rocket:
